    Restrict polarity alignment to its dominant axis, orient it toward the ray, and log ground truth.
    
    dualDerivedNorm now restricts the incident-angle (ray) term to whichever
    single axis the polar vector is dominant on before blending with the
    (unrestricted) position term, so off-axis ray motion can't dilute the
    alignment used for the commit-reflect-vs-permeate decision.
    
    Add Physics.polarityIncidentNormal: polar is baked (Polarization#bakeOctant)
    as "points toward the higher-impedance corner cluster", a fixed property of
    the octant independent of which side a given ray approaches from -- feeding
    that raw direction straight into grazeBend/permeationBend (which assume
    polNorm already faces the incoming ray) gets the bend backwards for roughly
    half of all approaches. polarityIncidentNormal per-axis sign-copies polNorm
    onto rayNorm (same idiom as permeationBend's own sign-copy) to guarantee it
    always faces the ray, and Cast's three grazeBend/permeationBend call sites
    now go through it instead of the raw baked polar direction.
    
    Add lastPolarVector/lastCommitWeight to Cast, threaded through Renderer ->
    CaptureBuffer.CapturedRay -> KaptureLogger (polarVec=/w= in the kapture
    log), so the next capture at a polarized boundary shows the raw polar
    vector and the actual pre-bend commit weight instead of requiring them to
    be reconstructed by hand from position data.

I dug through `run/logs/latest.log` (ray #51, the latest capture) and root-caused the polarity bug. Here's what I found, then a question about the phase-schedule idea.

**Homogeneous-octant polarity bug — confirmed root cause**

Ray #51 bounce #1 shows a `node=2³` cell labeled `material=air` with `Z==Zprev==426.9` (no blend happening) yet still logging `polar=0.866 polarVec=0.0000,8.0000,0.0000`. That's only possible if `NodeDescriptor.polar() != null` while `mostCommonImpedance() == leastCommonImpedance()` — a state `Polarization.bakeOctant`/`bakeAggregateDescriptor` should never produce on their own (both null out `polar` exactly when the impedance range collapses).

The actual defect is in `OctreeManager.growOctree` (`OctreeManager.java:222-249` for size-2, `:219-222` for size>2): it always bakes the multi-corner/aggregate descriptor (with whatever `polar` that computes) **before** checking whether the node is actually being pruned to a single homogeneous leaf (`valid`/`!heterogeneous`, decided by `sameAcousticCell`'s block-identity shortcut). When the pruning check and the impedance-based heterogeneity check disagree — e.g. `sameAcousticCell`'s `reference.getBlock() == sample.getBlock()` shortcut calls two corners "the same" without ever comparing their actual baked `Material`/impedance — a node that gets pruned to one material still carries the polarized descriptor computed from the corner differences the shortcut papered over. This is already flagged, unfixed, in `BranchVirtualLodCellPolarPurityTest.java`'s own doc comment as "a known follow-up issue, not under test here."

**Proposed fix**: when `growOctree` decides a node is homogeneous and prunes it (`valid` true at size 2, `!heterogeneous` at size>2), bake a plain non-polarized descriptor from that single material's own impedance (reusing the existing `bakeLeafDescriptor` helper) instead of the corner/aggregate bake. Only use the polarized bake when the node genuinely stays subdivided. Small, symmetric change at both call sites — no test currently locks in the buggy behavior (I checked `BranchNeighborAccessorTest`, `CastGetBlockCoarseBranchPurityTest`, `CastSmallFrustumAirBoundaryPurityTest` — none assert a pruned node keeps polarity).
